clue.text: Defender must hold line — sees areas of potential danger

indicators.note: the defender's word must hold, keep within it, the letter for line

parts.note: a back is a defending player in football or rugby
to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: A football commentator notes that a defender must hold the line while spotting danger zones.
explanation.definitionFit: Black spots are places, often on roads, where accidents or trouble keep happening.

clue.text: Dress up and lay it on thick

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for dress is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress

explanation.surface: A dandy dresses up flamboyantly and exaggerates everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast is to exaggerate one's own merits, laying the praise on heavily.

clue.text: I'm in a state, seeing spirit

indicators.note: the word I'm is placed in the phrase for a state

parts.note: a nation is a state
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being flustered, as if seeing a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness or vigour, the sense of spirit as energy.

clue.text: This should cut knot, with partner losing weight

parts.note: KN is the abbreviation for knot, a nautical speed

indicators.note: the partner's word loses the letter for weight

parts.note: a wife is a marriage partner

explanation.surface: Advice about a blade that cuts through a knot, said alongside a slimming spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is the obvious tool that would do cutting.

clue.text: Record crush

explanation.surface: A note about logging something and squashing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing something down puts it on record; a squelching retort humiliates and crushes someone.

clue.text: Administrator is bound to be heard here occasionally

indicators.note: the word for bound is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: trussed means tied up, bound

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word here is used

explanation.surface: An official is sure to be listened to in this place now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word. The second and fourth letters of HERE give EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee administers property or funds held in trust for others.

clue.text: Light mainly needed for metal band

indicators.note: most of the word for a light is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a torch is a portable light

explanation.surface: Mostly light is needed to make a band of metal shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is an ancient Celtic neck ring of twisted metal.

clue.text: Australia working with energy and gas

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia
on means working, operating
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Australia gets busy combining energy and natural gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen, a gas found high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Collusion of sanctimonious blue supporting Tories

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting words sit below the word for Tories

parts.note: Cons is short for Conservatives, the Tories
pi is slang for pious, sanctimonious
blue means risqué, racy

explanation.surface: Politicians plotting together in a priggish blue backing the Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy is a secret plot, people colluding together.

clue.text: Innocently hurry in case of call on unknown

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the unknown
the word for hurry goes in the outer letters of call
the case of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: haste means hurry
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone innocently rushes to answer a call from an unknown number.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastely means purely or virtuously, without sin.

clue.text: Excuse from politician sitting in first-class

indicators.note: the politician sits inside the first-class letters

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
Lib is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A politician travelling first class makes excuses for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse.

clue.text: Come down to earth, a little depressed

parts.note: a touch is a small amount
down means depressed, low

explanation.surface: Returning to reality, someone feels a bit gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft and spacecraft land when they reach the ground; the phrase means landing.

clue.text: A judge in Chelsea perhaps without shoes

indicators.note: a judge goes in the footwear

parts.note: a Chelsea boot is an ankle boot, so Chelsea is an example of a boot
a ref, referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: A referee at a Chelsea match oddly goes shoeless.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea looks like the football club; here it is a style of boot, a slip-on ankle boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being barefoot means having bare feet, wearing no footwear.

clue.text: Extent of leak by head of security

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to weep is to ooze or leak

explanation.surface: The security chief measures how far a data leak spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is a broad range or expanse, the extent of something.

clue.text: City look cheerful as soldiers must be accommodated

indicators.note: the words for as and soldiers must be housed within the smile

parts.note: to smile is to look cheerful
qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of
RE, Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Look happy, since troops need billeting in town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Square Mile is the nickname of the City of London, its financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: The City of London covers about one square mile, giving the district its nickname.

clue.text: Daughter wrong on question one — sitting pretty!

indicators.note: the daughter and wrong pieces come on, after, the first two

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A daughter sins on the first question yet ends up comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: Quids in is British slang for being in profit, a quid being a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in profit or well-off leaves you comfortably placed, in an enviable spot.

clue.text: Singular sort of English affliction

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: a sort of the word English is a rearranged version of it

explanation.surface: A peculiarly English kind of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingles is a painful viral skin disease, an affliction.

clue.text: One may vote in English reader

parts.note: a lector is a reader, as in church or a university

explanation.surface: A lecturer in English might cast a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector is a person entitled to vote in an election.

clue.text: Tease a little bit, upset, having lost book

indicators.note: the letters, once upset, are knocked into a new order
the phrase gives up the letter for book before the scramble

explanation.surface: Teasing someone a bit upsets them after a book goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B from A LITTLE BIT to leave ALITTLEIT, and 'upset' rearranges those nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse playfully, which is to tease.

clue.text: Cover not needed for smartest relations!

indicators.note: the outer letters, the cover, of the word for smartest are dropped

parts.note: jauntiest means most stylish, smartest

explanation.surface: The best-dressed can do without a hat or coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip J and T from JAUNTIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are relatives; the familiar plural form names these female relations.

clue.text: Amount charged for holding silver in stock

indicators.note: the silver goes in the word for stock

parts.note: a store is a stock or supply
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A jeweller's fee for keeping silver in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is the fee paid for keeping goods in a warehouse.

clue.text: Mysterious burial chamber with rich interior

parts.note: a crypt is an underground burial vault

indicators.note: the interior of the word rich is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A spooky tomb with luxurious furnishings inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means obscure or puzzling, having hidden meaning.

clue.text: City street full of good humour? The opposite!

indicators.note: one word is said to be full of another, signalling containment
the containment runs the other way: the street is inside the good humour

parts.note: cheer is good spirits, good humour

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a city street brims with merriment, then flipping the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester is a historic walled city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is the county town of Cheshire, an English cathedral city.

clue.text: Looking at, for example, protecting dark part of Chinese symbol

indicators.note: the example abbreviation wraps round, protecting, the other piece

parts.note: yin is the dark half of the yin-yang symbol

explanation.surface: Someone is studying the shaded half of a Chinese emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing something means watching or gazing at it closely.

clue.text: Still at home — finally leave for appointment

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the final letters of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: Sitting at home, someone finally sets off for an appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless or inactive, perfectly still.

clue.text: Clothing line worn by a lover troubled by son

indicators.note: the line is put on, worn, inside the shuffled letters
the words a lover, troubled, become disordered

explanation.surface: A distressed lover and son both wear a certain line of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' turns A LOVER into OVERAL, and 'worn by' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are protective garments worn over ordinary clothes.

clue.text: Book found by a sailor travelling north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A volume discovered by a seaman voyaging north.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps, a sailor's natural reading.

clue.text: Join fool for audition

indicators.note: the word is meant for listening, so its sound counts

parts.note: a nit is a fool, nitwit

explanation.surface: An idiot signs up for a talent-show tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a stage tryout; here it means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken bones are said to knit when they join together.

clue.text: Leaving fine leg antagonised will be awkward

indicators.note: what remains, the leavings, once ends are stripped from the phrase is the run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A fielder leaving his fine leg position angrily would be clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine leg is a fielding position in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace, clumsy.

clue.text: Find out king's name

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: Discover what the monarch is called.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to come to know it.

clue.text: Listeners will have time for right food

indicators.note: the word for listeners takes in a new letter
time stands for, replaces, the letter for right

parts.note: ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: An audience will have time for proper food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is slang for food, grub.

clue.text: A backward view of troublesome reports etc

indicators.note: troublesome letters are unruly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Looking back over a pile of bothersome reports and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospect is a survey of the past, looking back.
